newsitem.title: UK: UK electricity watchdog sets price caps on Grid.
newsitem.headline: UK electricity watchdog sets price caps on Grid.

text.p: Electricity watchdog OFFER set out final proposals for price controls on Britain's National Grid transmission system on Thursday which could mean savings for customers of one billion pounds ($1.57 billion) over four years.

OFFER's proposals include a one-off reduction in the first year from April 1, 1997 of 20 percent followed by a cap on price increases of four points below inflation, or RPI-4, for the following three years to 2001.
OFFER head Stephen Littlechild said domestic customers should see average price cuts of four pounds a year from the proposals.
In a statement, OFFER said National Grid stood to gain or lose up to 21 million pounds in 1997/98 depending on its success in responding to incentives in the proposals.
"It is a tough proposal but a realistic one," he said in an interview on BBC Radio news.
The final one-off cut proposed is at the bottom end of a 20-26 percent range outlined by OFFER in August. Those plans also called for curbs on future price changes of RPI-4.
National Grid shares eased in pre-market trading to be quoted a penny lower at 177-1/2 pence by 0717 GMT.

National Grid said it would review the proposals and respond to OFFER by October 30. If it finds the proposals unacceptable, OFFER head Stephen Littlechild said he would expect a referral to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission.
In August, National Grid described OFFER's plans as "contrived, illogical and inconsistent," and said revenues could be sliced by 200-300 million pounds in 1997-98.
Littlechild said he had listened to National Grid's representations on those proposals and made some modifications.

The latest proposals change the asset valuation basis to 4.15 billion pounds, up 150 million pounds from the basis in earlier proposals. OFFER said this reflected a lower attributed value of its Energis telecommunications business at flotation.
They also assume captial expenditure of 775 million pounds, 60 million pounds above earlier assumptions. ($1=.6385 Pound)
